newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedes lose faith in PM's promises - poll.
newsitem.headline: Swedes lose faith in PM's promises - poll.

text.p: Swedes have lost faith in Prime Minister Goran Persson's promises since he took office seven months ago, a new poll showed on Friday.
A Gallup poll, published in Swedish tabloid newspaper Expressen, found nine out of 10 Swedes did not think Persson could fulfil his key promise - to halve unemployment by the year 2000.
Unemployment is currently running at around 8.3 percent but Persson has pledged to cut this to 4.0 percent by 2000.
The poll also found two out of three people questioned, or 64 percent, did not believe even Persson believed his promise any longer.
"The result is a vote of no confidence in the prime minister," Expressen said.
Cutting unemployment was the key promise made by Persson in March when he succeeded Ingvar Carlsson. Carlsson resigned to spend more time with his family.
Persson also pledged to balance the budget by 1998.
Economists say the real rate of unemployment including people on state-run schemes is about 12 percent.
In recent weeks anger over the unemployment level and cuts in health services has triggered a series of protests around Sweden.
